PullRequest.Title: agentHost: Exclude SDK-native skills from directory discovery
PullRequest.Body:
## Problem

In Agent Host discovery mode, VS Code combines two Copilot runtime APIs that intentionally return different sets of data:

- `skills.getDiscoveryPaths()` returns directories where users can create skills, such as project, personal, and configured custom directories.
- `skills.discover()` returns every skill available to the runtime, including skills supplied by installed plugins and the runtime itself.

VS Code previously assumed that every item from `skills.discover()` belonged under a directory from `skills.getDiscoveryPaths()`. Copilot runtime 1.0.84-2 exposed that latent mismatch by returning installed-plugin skills. Because plugin and built-in skills do not have user-creatable discovery directories, VS Code created synthetic writable fallback directories for them and emitted an invariant error on every customization refresh:

`[SessionCustomizationDiscovery] BUG: customization '.../installed-plugins/.../SKILL.md' of type 'skill' is outside discovered directories`

In one recent Insiders session this repeated tens of thousands of times. The resulting directory entries were also projected into VS Code's synthetic session plugin even though plugin and built-in skills are SDK-native sources.

## Fix

Exclude skills whose SDK `source` is `plugin` or `builtin` before converting discovered skills into directory customizations.

This keeps the two ownership paths separate:

- SDK-native plugin and built-in skills remain owned and loaded by the Copilot runtime.
- Project, inherited, personal, and custom-directory skills continue to be represented by VS Code directory customizations.

The existing fallback and invariant error remain unchanged for directory-backed customizations that unexpectedly cannot be attributed to a discovery path. Using `excludeHostSkills` on the RPC request would not be appropriate because it would also hide legitimate personal and configured custom-directory skills.

## Testing

Added a regression test that returns plugin, built-in, and project skills from the SDK and verifies that:

- plugin and built-in skills are excluded from directory customizations;
- the project skill remains under its reported discovery directory; and
- no fallback error is emitted for the SDK-native skills.

Validation:

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionCustomizationDiscovery.test.ts` - 44 passing
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- pre-commit hygiene checks

(Written by Copilot)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed filesystem calls, their serialized placement, per-session critical-path caller, and F-by-D scaling are directly visible in the changed code. Exact latency depends on plugin count, contribution count, path depth, and filesystem speed, which is reflected in medium severity rather than lower mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For F unique files reported across installed plugins and ancestor depth D, the new root phase performs up to 3*F*D filesystem operations serially; deduplicating pluginRoots only happens after this cost. A plugin with many agents/rules/skills therefore repeats the same ancestor probes for each child.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased session-creation and customization-refresh latency from serialized filesystem I/O
Findings.PreviousBehavior: SDK-native plugin agents and rules were converted from the SDK discovery response without filesystem root probing; plugin skills incurred their existing skill-file parse, but no ancestor walk was performed for every reported plugin child.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every unique SDK-reported plugin agent, rule, or skill is now sent through findPluginRoot before roots are deduplicated. That helper performs up to three awaited filesystem existence checks at each ancestor, and the outer loop awaits files one at a time.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added call `const root = await this.findPluginRoot(file, token);` at line 771 introduces one serialized ancestor walk per SDK-reported plugin file; the added findPluginRoot implementation at lines 807-824 performs up to three awaited existence checks at every ancestor before roots are deduplicated.
Findings.Title: Cache plugin-root discovery across reported plugin files
Findings.Impact: Creating a Copilot agent session with SDK-installed plugins now waits for these probes through createSession -> getChatCustomizations -> getCustomizationsSettled -> discover. Workspace customization changes and root-config changes rerun the same uncached work, so plugins with many contributions can also delay refreshes and slash-command customization reads.
Findings.Evidence: SessionDiscoveredEntry is per session and its initial refresh is awaited by getCustomizationsSettled; AgentService awaits getChatCustomizations while creating the initial session snapshot. In the added code, toPluginCustomizations loops over every pluginFiles entry and awaits findPluginRoot, whose loop awaits three IFileService.exists calls per ancestor. ResourceSet removes duplicate file URIs, not the many distinct files belonging to one plugin, and pluginRoots is populated only after each full walk.
Findings.Recommendation: Memoize visited ancestor directories to their resolved plugin root (including negative results) for the duration of a discovery, so all files under one plugin share one walk; preserve cancellation and manifest-format checks. Grouping SDK results by a cached root before parsing also keeps root-level work proportional to installed plugins rather than contributed files.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: SDK-native plugin customizations were treated as directory-backed items even though their paths were outside all SDK discovery directories, causing the fallback invariant error to be emitted once per such customization on every discovery refresh.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: The PR records a recent session emitting the invariant error tens of thousands of times, creating excessive logging work and log I/O during customization refreshes.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added source check diverts plugin-owned agents into plugin projection instead of directory conversion (with corresponding checks for rules and skills), so these SDK-native items no longer hit the per-customization fallback error path; the remaining fallback diagnostic is also lowered from error to trace.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before the change, discoverAgents/rules/skills returned plugin-owned children to toDirectoryCustomizations; when no discovery directory contained them, base line 875 logged an error inside the per-customization loop. Added line 639 identifies plugin agents before insertion, corresponding added source checks handle rules and skills, and the new plugin projection keeps them out of that fallback path. blame identifies the SDK-discovery change that introduced the old mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or restore a Copilot agent session while SDK-installed plugins contribute agents, rules, or skills
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AgentService awaits provider.getChatCustomizations for the initial session snapshot; that awaits SessionPluginController.getCustomizationsSettled, whose per-session SessionDiscoveredEntry waits for discover and the newly added plugin-root/projection work. The new root probes and plugin parsing run after the initial Promise.all discovery phase, so they directly extend session creation rather than running off-path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copilot SDK getDiscoveryPaths/discover RPCs for agents, instructions, and skills
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A fixed set of SDK RPCs per discovery, with discover calls issued concurrently; response size contains F effective plugin files plus non-plugin customizations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK discovery RPCs were already required before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These RPCs must complete before plugin projection and the settled customization snapshot can complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe `.plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, and `plugin.json` while walking ancestors for each reported plugin file
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 3*F*D existence/resolve operations, serialized; root deduplication occurs only after every file has paid its walk.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No plugin-root ancestor probing occurred; SDK plugin agents/rules used response metadata directly, while plugin skills only incurred their skill-file parse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after SDK discovery and blocks construction of the initial customization snapshot.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Detect each plugin format, read its manifest, and parse all plugin component directories/files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full parse per deduplicated root P, serialized across roots; detectPluginFormat and readPluginManifest are also called immediately outside parsePlugin, which repeats both internally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no whole-plugin parse for SDK-native plugins in this path; agents/rules were mapped from SDK metadata and skills were parsed individually.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the settled customization snapshot after root discovery; internal component readers perform directory resolves, realpaths, and skill/agent file reads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover hooks and resolve/watch configured customization directories
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Proportional to configured workspace/user discovery roots and fixed hook locations, with resolveAll batching for watcher roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in the initial discovery Promise.all and was already part of the settled snapshot path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P installed plugins, F distinct SDK-reported plugin contribution files after ResourceSet deduplication, and D ancestors from each contribution to its plugin root. Root lookup scales as up to 3*F*D filesystem checks, followed by P whole-plugin parses.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: SDK agent/rule/skill discovery, hook discovery, and watcher update begin concurrently. The new root lookup is serialized across all F files, each ancestor's format probes are short-circuit serial, and plugin roots are then parsed serially across P; parsePlugin parallelizes its five component readers internally. Separate sessions own separate discovery entries and can perform this work concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Discovered directory paths are cached within one SessionDiscoveredEntry, but plugin-file-to-root results and parsed SDK-native plugins are not cached. Every new/restored session has a cold entry, and every later refresh repeats root discovery and parsing; warm OS filesystem caches may reduce duration but do not reduce operation count. There is no cross-session coalescing or negative root cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the per-session awaited call path, serialized filesystem operations, and F-by-D scaling are explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact added milliseconds depend on installed plugin count, contribution count, nesting depth, filesystem latency, and OS cache warmth. Typical small plugin sets may hide the cost, while contribution-heavy plugins or slower/remote home filesystems amplify it.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity boundary fan-out: cache ancestor-to-root results so work scales with plugins rather than plugin files. The richer plugin projection may require a per-root parse, but it does not require repeating root discovery per child.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh open-session customizations after a watched workspace/user customization change or root configuration change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A file watcher or root-config event schedules a 100 ms debounced SessionDiscoveredEntry refresh. The refresh reruns discover, including the new plugin root probes and parses, before publishing the customization update. Calls such as skill slash-command candidate retrieval that arrive while this refresh is pending await getCustomizationsSettled; otherwise the work is on the customization-update critical path rather than the message-rendering path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three concurrent discover RPCs per affected session and settled refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The refresh already repeated these RPCs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the refreshed customization set is compared and published.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeat per-file ancestor manifest probes and per-root plugin parsing
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 3*F*D root probes plus P plugin scans per affected session after each debounced refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Refreshes did not locate and reparse SDK-native plugin roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delays refreshed customization publication and any concurrent settled customization reader.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The same F plugin files, D ancestor depth, and P plugin roots per affected session; a user-home change can affect N open sessions, producing N independent copies of the work after per-entry debouncing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Events within one entry are coalesced by Delayer and an in-flight refresh is canceled/replaced. There is no coalescing across open sessions; each session entry can issue its SDK RPCs and filesystem work concurrently, while each entry serializes root walks and root parses internally.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The `_discoveredDirectories` cache avoids repeated getDiscoveryPaths calls within one entry, but SDK discover calls, plugin-root walks, plugin parsing, and their negative results are repeated on each settled refresh. The 100 ms debounce limits event frequency but does not reuse plugin results across refreshes or sessions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: watcher/config events are wired directly to the per-session refresh, no plugin cache exists, and the changed filesystem work is awaited.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously open sessions and frequency of relevant watched changes vary. Debouncing bounds bursts within one session, but shared user customization changes can still fan out across sessions.
Scenarios.Verdict: Same reported fan-out applies. No separate finding is needed because the trigger and correction share the identical changed mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and traced the production discovery path, session creation/refresh callers, parser filesystem operations, caches, and concurrency. Submitted one medium-severity finding for serialized per-plugin-file ancestor probing. Also recorded that the PR fixes the prior per-customization invariant-log fan-out introduced by abfa1b66f7b6a328fbb69f5292dee98c36290b06.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
